---
title: "Calculator"
description: "Roughly how much more tax an unmarried couple in Ireland pays than a married one, under 2027 rules."
resources:
  - tax-rules.js
---

Part of [Cohabitation in Ireland](index.qmd). How each tax works, with sources, is on [The cost of not marrying](cost.qmd).

Fill in the boxes to see roughly how much more tax you pay because you aren't married. It's an estimate, not tax advice.

```{=html}
<form id="mc-form" class="mc-form" onsubmit="return false">
  <label>Your income (€ a year) <input type="number" inputmode="numeric" id="a" min="0" step="1000" value="60000"></label>
  <label>Your partner's income (€ a year) <input type="number" inputmode="numeric" id="b" min="0" step="1000" value="0"></label>
  <label>Years you expect to be together <input type="number" inputmode="numeric" id="y" min="0" max="80" step="1" value="30"></label>
  <label>What one of you would leave the other (€), such as your share of the home and savings <input type="number" inputmode="numeric" id="inh" min="0" step="10000" value="300000"></label>
  <label>Your stage of life (optional)
    <select id="stage">
      <option value="">Choose one</option>
      <option value="young">Raising young children</option>
      <option value="children">Raising older children</option>
      <option value="none">No children</option>
      <option value="later">Children grown up, or retired</option>
    </select>
  </label>
</form>

<div class="mc-result" aria-live="polite">
  <p class="mc-total-label">Not being married would cost you about</p>
  <p class="mc-total" id="mc-total">€0</p>
  <p id="mc-income"></p>
  <p id="mc-inherit"></p>
  <p id="mc-stage" hidden></p>
</div>

<script src="tax-rules.js"></script>
<script>
(function () {
  var T = window.MarriageTax;
  var eur = function (x) { return "€" + Math.round(x).toLocaleString("en-IE"); };
  function val(id) { var v = parseFloat(document.getElementById(id).value); return isFinite(v) && v > 0 ? v : 0; }
  var stageNotes = {
    young: "If one of you is at home with the children, a married couple could also claim the Home Carer Tax Credit, worth up to €2,050 a year, so your real gap may be bigger than this.",
    children: "If one of you works part time or stays at home, a married couple could also claim the Home Carer Tax Credit, worth up to €2,050 a year, so your real gap may be bigger than this.",
    none: "Without children together, you count as qualified cohabitants after five years living together, rather than two. That is the test for the Bereaved Partner's Pension, and for applying to the court for provision from a partner's estate.",
    later: "At this stage the inheritance tax matters most. Since 2025 a surviving qualified cohabitant can get the State's Bereaved Partner's Pension, but some occupational schemes, like the civil service scheme in the Jones case, still pay a pension only to a spouse."
  };
  function update() {
    var a = val("a"), b = val("b"), y = Math.round(val("y")), inh = val("inh");
    var yearly = T.incomeTaxGap(a, b);
    var cat = T.inheritanceTaxCohabitant(inh);
    document.getElementById("mc-total").textContent = eur(yearly * y + cat);
    document.getElementById("mc-income").textContent = yearly > 0
      ? "You pay " + eur(yearly) + " a year more income tax than a married couple on the same incomes. Over " + y + " years that adds up to " + eur(yearly * y) + "."
      : "On these incomes you pay the same income tax as a married couple.";
    document.getElementById("mc-inherit").textContent = cat > 0
      ? "If one of you died, the other would pay " + eur(cat) + " in inheritance tax. A husband, wife or civil partner would pay nothing."
      : "On this amount there would be no inheritance tax to pay.";
    var note = stageNotes[document.getElementById("stage").value];
    var el = document.getElementById("mc-stage");
    el.hidden = !note;
    el.textContent = note || "";
  }
  ["a", "b", "y", "inh", "stage"].forEach(function (id) {
    document.getElementById(id).addEventListener("input", update);
    document.getElementById(id).addEventListener("change", update);
  });
  update();
})();
</script>
```

## What it assumes

The calculator uses the 2027 tax rates, bands and credits from Budget 2027 for every year, with no inflation or pay rises, and treats both incomes as wages. A married couple pays whichever is lower, joint assessment or being taxed separately. USC and PRSI are left out because they are charged on each person separately whether you are married or not.

The Home Carer Tax Credit, worth up to €2,050 a year to married couples and civil partners, is left out, so the real gap can be bigger.

The inheritance tax figure assumes the partner who inherits has had no earlier gifts or inheritances that count towards the same €22,000 threshold, and that no relief applies. The [dwelling house exemption](cost.qmd#inheritance) can cover the family home if strict conditions are met, and money awarded by a court under the Cohabitants Act 2010 is tax free.

The calculator doesn't include capital gains tax, which an unmarried partner can also face when they give the other an asset such as a share in a property. That's explained on [The cost of not marrying](cost.qmd#capital-gains).

The rules are in [`tax-rules.js`](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/blob/main/cohabitation/tax-rules.js), with a source for each number, and are updated after each Budget.
